newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exporters say exports at $2 bln in August.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exporters say exports at $2 bln in August.

text.p: Turkey's biggest exporters' body said data obtained from exporters' unions showed total exports at $2.01 billion in August, up seven percent from a year ago.
The Turkish Exporters Assembly (TIM) estimated exports in the first eight months of 1996 at $14.89 billion, up 5.7 percent from the same 1995 period.

"Exports have shown an uptrend at small rates and with volatility. It is possible (for Turkey) to miss the year-end export target if appropriate measures are not taken in the short term," TIM chairman Okan Oguz said in a statement.
Official 1996 targets are $25 billion of exports and $41 billion of imports.
TIM said the top item readywear exports which had previously been on a downtrend, rose 10 percent to an unofficial $685.7 million last month, compared to August 1995.

Last month, exports of iron and steel fell 12 percent to $207.4 million, textile and textile raw material exports rose seven percent to $181.2 million, electronics exports were up nine percent to $137.2 million, versus August 1995.
Meanwhile, automotive and parts exports leapt 26 percent to $123.7 million and chemicals jumped 43 percent to $168.5 million, according to figures released by TIM.
Official data put Turkey's trade deficit in January at $1.29 billion, up sharply from $547 million a year earlier.
The release of official trade data has been delayed by technical difficulties arising from Turkey's customs union with the European Union since January 1.
